races.paceDynamic: Diamond Exchange will lead uncontested from the gates with Dutch Gold and Mr Rango settling prominently behind. The pace will be genuine but not frantic over this 1m2f trip, as Diamond Exchange has proven he can sustain his front-running style without pressure. The large field of mainly hold-up horses will bunch up in midfield and at the rear, creating a wall of traffic problems turning for home. This race shape strongly favours front-runners and prominent racers who can avoid the inevitable congestion, with hold-up horses facing a significant tactical disadvantage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Front Runner Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Diamond Exchange maintains his lead without serious pressure through the middle stages
scenarios.body: He can kick clear turning for home while the packed field behind struggles with traffic problems, allowing him to hold on despite his modest rating. His proven stamina at this trip and recent Dundalk win give him the tools to capitalize.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the hold-up horses get severely hampered in the home straight scramble
scenarios.body: Dutch Gold or Mr Rango can track the pace cleanly and pounce when Diamond Exchange weakens, avoiding the chaos further back that traps the better-rated horses. The tactical advantage outweighs the rating differential.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Strong Finisher Finds Gap
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses significantly in the final two furlongs and gaps appear
scenarios.body: Abbey Actress or Diego El Queso can unleash their superior class late, with Abbey Actress particularly dangerous given her soft ground form and recent C&D third. Their higher ratings tell if they get racing room.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Allows Outsider Through
scenarios.trigger: If multiple fallers or severe interference creates unusual circumstances
scenarios.body: A horse like Thatwilldoso or Amplitude could sneak through on the rails while the fancied runners get blocked, though this requires significant luck and multiple things going wrong for the market leaders.

watchPoints.text: Diamond Exchange must be monitored for early fractions - if he goes too fast early he becomes very vulnerable late
Abbey Actress needs close attention for market support given her soft ground ability and recent course form
The pace battle between Dutch Gold and Mr Rango could compromise both if they get into a speed duel behind Diamond Exchange
Switch From Diesel's betting market will reveal stable confidence after his lengthy 164-day absence
Any significant drift on Diego El Queso would be concerning given Colin Keane's strong recent form and the horse's Curragh second

races.paceDynamic: Mississippi River and Norwalk Havoc will contest the early lead, with both confirmed front-runners likely to engage from the start. This honest gallop will create a genuine test over the mile trip, particularly on the yielding ground which should emphasize stamina. The prominent runners like Mutasarref and Expanded will sit close behind the leaders, while the large contingent of hold-up horses including The Lion In Winter, Jancis, and Lord Massusus will rely on the pace being strong enough to set up their finishing kicks. This race shape strongly favours the prominent/pressing horses who can avoid the early battle but still maintain position, as they can capitalize on a strong pace without expending too much early energy.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Excel
scenarios.trigger: If Mississippi River and Norwalk Havoc set a solid gallop without one dropping out early
scenarios.body: The genuine pace allows prominent runners to time their challenge perfectly, avoiding the early speed battle while staying close enough to strike. Mutasarref's course expertise and Expanded's Ballydoyle polish prove decisive in this tactical position.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Prevail
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes overly fierce between the two front-runners
scenarios.body: The strong gallop perfectly sets up the race for closers who can unleash devastating finishing kicks. The Lion In Winter's class and Jancis's proven Group-level ability shine through late on the yielding ground.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Survives
scenarios.trigger: If one of Mississippi River or Norwalk Havoc gets first run and maintains their advantage
scenarios.body: The leader gets enough of a breather mid-race to sustain their effort, with the soft ground helping their stamina reserves. Mississippi River's superior class tells in a bold front-running display.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Improver Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the main fancies fail to fire and the pace collapses into a sprint finish
scenarios.body: An unexposed or improving type capitalizes on a messy race where the favorites cancel each other out. Tokenomics or Ribee could exploit the chaos with their recent winning form.

watchPoints.text: Mississippi River and Norwalk Havoc setting unsustainable early fractions that compromise both front-runners completely
The Lion In Winter getting boxed in during the crucial final two furlongs given his reliance on a clear finishing run
Mutasarref being unable to cope with the yielding ground despite his course record, as his best form came on faster surfaces
Expanded showing rust from his lengthy absence in the crucial final furlong despite traveling strongly throughout
Tokenomics and Ribee both running career-best races if the pace sets up perfectly for late-closing types

races.paceDynamic: Some Good Men Gone is the only confirmed front runner and will get an uncontested lead in this small field of nine. With most runners adopting prominent or hold-up tactics, he'll dictate fractions without early pressure, creating a sustainable gallop that builds gradually. The lack of pace pressure means the race will develop into a sprint finish from the 2f pole, with horses needing to time their runs perfectly on the yielding ground. This tactical setup strongly favours horses with proven finishing kicks who can stay close enough to strike, making hold-up performers and strong finishers the profiles to follow.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Lead Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Some Good Men Gone gets soft fractions and stays the trip
scenarios.body: He builds an insurmountable lead as the held-up horses leave their runs too late on the testing ground. The lack of early pace means front runners can steal a march when the finish develops.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Hero Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes truly crawling and sets up a sprint finish
scenarios.body: Zipster and Star Mind benefit from their patient tactics as the race becomes a dash from the home turn. Their finishing kicks prove superior when the field bunches up late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If Teffian Warrior or Urban War track the leader closely throughout
scenarios.body: They get first run on Some Good Men Gone turning for home and have enough left to repel late challengers. The prominent position proves ideal when others are caught too far back.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Completely
scenarios.trigger: If Some Good Men Gone stops quickly and the field comes to a crawl
scenarios.body: The race becomes a lottery sprint where any horse with a turn of foot can win from an impossible position. Form and ratings become irrelevant in the resulting scramble.

watchPoints.text: Some Good Men Gone could steal this if he gets uncontested fractions and the field leaves their runs too late
Zipster showed solid recent form when third at Gowran and his hold-up style suits if the pace becomes pedestrian
Teffian Warrior returns from long break but his Galway form gives him a chance if handling the step up in distance
Staywitherjohnny and Your Out Of Line both carry warnings about fading in the finish which could prove costly
The yielding ground may play differently than expected, potentially hampering those who need quick ground to show their best

races.name: FM104 "Giddy Up" Handicap

runners_data.name: Greek Flower
runners_data.note: Hold-up style faces traffic nightmare in 17-runner field, 164 days off adds rustiness concern
runners_data.comment: Nothing since back-to-back wins in 2023; creditable fifth on first try at 7f in Nov'
runners_data.spotlight: Back-to-back winner in 2023 in a 5f Navan maiden (soft) and a 6f Curragh handicap off 70 (heavy); nothing since then but creditable fifth at the Curragh in November on her first try at this trip in a first-time hood and tongue tie (left off now).

runners_data.name: Anvika
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with quick 3-day turnaround, needs serious pace collapse to be effective from rear
runners_data.comment: This comes quick enough since finishing 7.75l behind Vega's Muse here last time
runners_data.spotlight: Turf and AW winner was 7.75l behind Vega's Muse at this venue three days ago when finishing in midfield (1m, good to yielding); this comes quick enough and others preferred.

runners_data.name: Glory To Be
runners_data.note: Prominent style suits race shape perfectly, form figures show consistency at this level

runners_data.name: Free Solo
runners_data.note: Prominent runner but 9-year-old legs may not handle the tactical battle with six other prominent horses
runners_data.comment: Added sixth win at Roscommon in Aug'; not at best since and last of 13 on AW latest
runners_data.spotlight: Added his sixth win when landing a Roscommon handicap in August (7.5f, good) off 6lb lower; not at his best in runs since and finished last of 13 at Dundalk last time.

runners_data.name: I Bid You Ajou
runners_data.note: Prominent style fits but 7lb claiming jockey Joseph Harnett lacks experience for this tactical puzzle
runners_data.comment: Put three wins together last summer at Fairyhouse on good ground; second on AW last time
runners_data.spotlight: Strung three consecutive wins together last summer at Fairyhouse in a claimer and two handicaps on good ground; remains 2lb above his last winning mark but it was a very positive seasonal return at Dundalk two weeks ago when a 0.5l runner-up under today's rider; in the mix but won't want any rain.

runners_data.name: Chester Nimitz
runners_data.note: Prominent runner making stable debut for Gerard O'Leary, 189 days off creates fitness doubt
runners_data.comment: Won final start for Noel Meade in Navan m'den; not discounted on stable debut
runners_data.spotlight: Won his final start for Noel Meade in a Navan maiden in October (6f, yielding) under a front-running ride; makes stable debut now and not discounted.

runners_data.name: Vega's Muse
runners_data.note: Prominent style ideally suited, 5lb claiming Keithen Kennedy rode confidently when winning 3 days ago

runners_data.name: Pebble Island
runners_data.note: Hold-up style against 17 runners spells trouble, 225 days off makes this a tough return
runners_data.comment: Second in four-horse m'den was best run for Crisfords; little success hurdling recently
runners_data.spotlight: One-time 200,000gns yearling whose second placing in a four-horse maiden at Redcar marked a highlight from seven starts for the Crisfords; sent hurdling for his last two runs for new yard with little success.

runners_data.name: Thru And Thru
runners_data.note: Sole front runner gives him tactical advantage, but may lack class to hold off better horses

runners_data.name: Amemri
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse faces traffic problems, first reserve status suggests connections not overly confident
runners_data.comment: Reserve; back to form when winning on AW last month; decent effort over 6f latest
runners_data.spotlight: First reserve; back to form when recording a tenth win under rules' at Dundalk last month (7f); 6f perhaps a bit sharp back at Dundalk last time and was hampered turning in; not totally ruled out with a run.

runners_data.name: Goal Exceeded
runners_data.note: Hold-up style problematic in big field, 164-day break adds another layer of concern

runners_data.name: Verhoyen
runners_data.note: Prominent early but warning signs show he fades in the finish, 11-year-old veteran losing his edge
runners_data.comment: Last season's campaign was fruitless; mark dropping but not getting any younger
runners_data.spotlight: Seven-time winner on turf, but last season's campaign was fruitless; mark is at an all-time low but not getting any younger and record suggests he'll improve from his first time out.

runners_data.name: Senna's Girl
runners_data.note: Hold-up style needs gaps that won't appear, Diego Lima lacks tactical experience for this scenario
runners_data.comment: Winless from 12 and tailed off in Irish Lincoln last time; others more appealing
runners_data.spotlight: No wins from 12 but went close over 7f at the Curragh in November (heavy); raced from 5lb outside the handicap in the Irish Lincolnshire last time when tailed off (1m, heavy); tongue tie goes on now but others make more appeal.

runners_data.name: Finsceal Annie

runners_data.comment: Won two C&D races within a week last year; worth a look back here off 10lb higher
runners_data.spotlight: Won two races within a week here last year over C&D on different ground types; some good efforts at Laytown and Dundalk since then; beaten 8l in an AW handicap when last seen in November (1m); 10lb higher since last winning mark but worth a look back at this track.

runners_data.name: Hugo's Girl
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with 5lb claiming jockey, needs complete pace collapse to feature from rear

runners_data.name: Thaloria
runners_data.note: Prominent style could work but poor recent form figures suggest she's going the wrong way

runners_data.name: Proleek Prince
runners_data.note: Prominent runner but 140 days off and poor recent form make him hard to fancy
runners_data.comment: Turf winner off this mark in 2024; struggled last term; not many positives in latest run
runners_data.spotlight: Punchestown handicap winner in September 2024 off this mark (1m, good) and added an AW win at Dundalk later that year; struggled on turf last season and not many positives in his 8l tenth at Dundalk when last seen in November.

races.paceDynamic: Thru And Thru provides the sole confirmed front runner and should dictate a measured pace without pressure early. Seven horses want the prominent positions (Glory To Be, Free Solo, I Bid You Ajou, Chester Nimitz, Vega's Muse, Verhoyen, Thaloria), creating serious congestion and traffic problems from 3f out on this 7f trip. The large field of hold-up horses (Greek Flower, Anvika, Pebble Island, Amemri, Goal Exceeded, Senna's Girl, Finsceal Annie, Hugo's Girl) will be funneling through limited gaps in the final furlong. This race shape strongly favors prominent racers who can secure clear runs and avoid the inevitable traffic chaos that will engulf the hold-up brigade.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent group can settle without early skirmishing and secure clear runs
scenarios.body: The uncontested leader Thru And Thru sets it up perfectly for the prominent pack to sweep past in the final 2f while the hold-up horses get caught in traffic. Those with tactical pace avoid the carnage behind.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Finds Gap
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent congestion creates enough early pace and one hold-up horse finds a clear passage
scenarios.body: The early tactical battle between seven prominent runners creates genuine pace for the first time, allowing a strong closer like Greek Flower or Anvika to exploit the gaps. Split-second timing decides the outcome.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If Thru And Thru gets completely uncontested fractions and kicks clear turning in
scenarios.body: With no genuine pace pressure early, the leader gets soft sectionals and has enough left to hold off the late challenge when the field finally organizes. The prominent pack hesitates too long to make their moves.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Produces Outsider
scenarios.trigger: If the traffic problems are so severe that most fancied runners get hampered
scenarios.body: The 17-runner field creates a complete scramble in the final 2f with multiple hard-luck stories, allowing a horse like Hugo's Girl or Goal Exceeded to emerge from the chaos with a clear run. Pure luck decides the winner.

watchPoints.text: Massive traffic problems developing 3f out when seven prominent horses and ten hold-up runners all need the same racing room
Thru And Thru could steal this if he gets completely uncontested fractions with no early pace pressure
Vega's Muse and Glory To Be have the tactical pace to avoid trouble but need their jockeys to be alert early
Chester Nimitz making stable debut after 189 days off - market support would be significant
Greek Flower and Anvika need genuine early pace from the prominent group to set up their hold-up style

runners_data.spotlight: Eight-time winner, but 0-10 at this venue; a lot of improvement needed based on two runs Curragh runs this season.

runners_data.name: Romantic War
runners_data.note: Lone leader with fading tendencies will set sustainable pace unchallenged

runners_data.spotlight: Still a maiden after 22 outings; respectable run on final 2025 turf start when third of 15 at Galway (7f, heavy); tailed off at Bellewstown in first run this year (1m, soft); blinkers go on now.

races.paceDynamic: Romantic War is the only confirmed front-runner and will dictate a sustainable early gallop without pressure. Seven horses wanting prominent positions (She's Ideal, Sedro Woolley, Twotolose, Rock Basher, Brains, Mullacash Buzz, Jazzy Dancer) will create significant congestion 2-3 furlongs out as they jostle for position behind the leader. The large field of hold-up horses (Zabriskie Point, Roman Harry, Mogwli, Methgal, Cannonball Queen, Kitty Bear, Sea Fort, Exceeding, Chipsrdown) will find limited room in the straight as traffic builds. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can secure good positions early and avoid the inevitable shuffle back.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Power Play
scenarios.trigger: If the seven prominent runners sort themselves out cleanly behind Romantic War without interference
scenarios.body: She's Ideal and Brains can utilize their tactical speed to secure ideal positions and kick clear when the pace lifts. The hold-up brigade gets caught in traffic as the prominent group spreads across the track.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Traffic Chaos Ensues
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent group gets bunched and creates a wall effect turning for home
scenarios.body: The pace collapse allows late runners like Methgal and Roman Harry to weave through and capitalize on superior finishing kicks. Those trapped behind the wall of prominent horses surrender crucial lengths.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Romantic War Stays
scenarios.trigger: If the lone leader maintains his gallop deeper than usual without folding
scenarios.body: The uncontested leader holds on grimly while the chasing pack arrives too late after sorting out their traffic problems. Second and third come from the prominent group who had clear runs.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Complete Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If Romantic War stops badly and the prominent group goes too slow early
scenarios.body: The entire field comes with one run and it becomes a pure sprint finish where the strongest stayers prevail. Hold-up horses with the best turn of foot sweep past the lot.

watchPoints.text: Romantic War could dictate fractions too slow early then compound traffic problems by staying longer than expected
She's Ideal and Brains clash for the same prominent position which could compromise both chances
The seven prominent runners create a cavalry charge scenario 2f out that stops several in their tracks
Methgal's recent good form makes him the hold-up horse most likely to find gaps
Watch for Jazzy Dancer to get first run on the prominent group with his 3lb claimer's assistance
